blocks.x: Product fleets in the field managed as products: OTA updates that never brick, telemetry that earns its bandwidth, support APIs your service desk can actually use — and firmware attack surfaces treated with the same gates as your cloud.
A connected product is a promise your support org has to keep

A connected product is a fleet you promised to keep working: the coffee machine in 40,000 kitchens, the charger in 200 supermarkets, the pump at 900 sites. The engineering is fleet product management — OTA with staged waves and rollback, telemetry budgets that earn their bandwidth, and diagnostics deep enough that support resolves cases before the customer finishes the call.
Security arrives by design: device identity, signed firmware, and the update path as the most-defended surface, because OTA is also the attack path.
Below: the failure modes that turn product fleets into liabilities, the reference architecture of fleet management, and the console that keeps firmware current safely.
Four failure modes that turn product fleets into liabilities
Each of these surfaces as a support crisis or a security headline — the countermeasures make updates safe by design and telemetry earn its keep.

widgets.title: The device platform — click nodes for the fleet contract

nodes.label: Secure element
nodes.detail: Root identity in hardware — device keys generated in the SE, certificates chained to the fleet CA; an identity that cannot be cloned is the platform's floor.

nodes.label: Firmware & A/B slots
nodes.detail: Signed updates staged to the inactive slot, health-checked, switched on proof — rollback is automatic on watchdog failure.

nodes.label: Desired-state shadow
nodes.detail: Each device holds its desired state offline; the fleet plane reconciles on connect — connectivity gaps never corrupt configuration.

nodes.label: OTA orchestration
nodes.detail: Cohort campaigns with canary gates, soak clocks and automatic halt on health regression — 48k devices update in nine days without heroics.

nodes.label: Entitlement engine
nodes.detail: Feature flags per device per contract tier, synced to billing — the fleet is monetizable because the entitlements are machine-readable.

nodes.label: Product telemetry
nodes.detail: Usage and health streams feeding the roadmap — churn signals, feature adoption and failure modes, aggregated with consent.

nodes.label: Fleet security
nodes.detail: Anomaly detection on device behavior (unexpected egress, credential anomalies), revocation at the CA — a compromised device is one certificate away from contained.

widgets.note: Click nodes for the contract each layer carries. The secure element is where trust starts — everything else inherits from it.

Firmware-security governance overlay
Signing keys, secure boot and vulnerability response run on the same gates as the cloud: CVE response waves ship within the signed SLA, and the firmware SBOM is maintained as a product artifact.

items: Unsigned firmware cannot reach a device

blocks.x: Telemetry earns its bandwidth by review: each signal is re-justified quarterly against the decisions it informs — signals without decisions are dropped, and the savings are real money at fleet scale.
